title: Shift square of the strict-system compactification projection composite
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $t$, and put $A_n=R/t^n$, $n\geq1$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type morphism between separated finite-type $k$-schemes, and fix a compactification $c=(X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{p_c}Y)$ with $j$ quasi-compact open and $p_c$ proper [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. On the small pro-etale sites put $B_{n,W}=(A_n)_W$. Let $\mathscr S_W$ be the category of strict semilinear $B_{\bullet,W}$-module systems with quotient transitions, and use its ordinary unbounded derived category [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Use the simultaneous ringed-diagram-site operations $P_v$, $S_{p_c}$, $J_j$ and derived system tensor of [lem-sf-integral-compactification-system-realization], with their canonical cochain-shift comparisons, and the signed second tensor comparison of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Put $\mathcal F_c=S_{p_c}J_j$. For $M\in D(\mathscr S_X)$ and $N\in D(\mathscr S_Y)$ let $\operatorname{PF}^{\mathrm{sys},c}_{M,N}$ be the specified composite
$$\mathcal F_cM\otimes^LN\xrightarrow{\pi_{p_c;J_jM,N}}S_{p_c}(J_jM\otimes^LP_{p_c}N)\xrightarrow{S_{p_c}(\delta)}S_{p_c}J_j(M\otimes^LP_jP_{p_c}N)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal F_c(M\otimes^LP_fN).$$
Here $\pi$ is the counit-defined proper projection mate of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact], $\delta$ is the open-unit-normalized tensor map of [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization], and the last arrow uses canonical pullback composition; these are precisely the system counterparts of the composite in [def-exchange-projection]. Define $F_M(N)=\mathcal F_cM\otimes^LN$ and $H_M(N)=\mathcal F_c(M\otimes^LP_fN)$. For every integer $r$, their canonical composite shift comparisons satisfy
$$s_H^{(r)}\circ\operatorname{PF}^{\mathrm{sys},c}_{M,N[r]}=\operatorname{PF}^{\mathrm{sys},c}_{M,N}[r]\circ s_F^{(r)}.$$
The proper factor and the open factor separately satisfy their corresponding shift squares, and the pullback-composition comparison commutes with shift. These are identities of derived system maps before evaluation, restriction of scalars or total inverse limit, for the quotient transitions of the same simultaneous models. The assertion includes normalized systems with bounded constructible finite-Tor levels [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower, def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude] and does not assert invertibility of the general projection map.

proof.text: Work on the simultaneous ringed diagram sites. By [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections], $\mathscr S_W$ is the module category over the ring object $B_{\bullet,W}$ in the inverse-sequence topos, and $P_v\dashv S_v$ and tensor are actual operations on its unbounded derived category. The arbitrary-ring-system clause of [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization] supplies a small diagram-site presentation and the open-unit-normalized $\delta$. Thus the ringed-topos theorem [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact] applies to the diagram-site morphism induced by $p_c$, with $E=J_jM$. Its $L,R,\alpha$ are exactly $P_{p_c},S_{p_c},\pi_{p_c;J_jM,-}$: both projection maps are the transpose of $(\varepsilon_{J_jM}\otimes1)\mu$. The exact inverse image has the constant-system structural ring identification, so no extension-of-scalars flatness is needed.

source.place: Tags 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product), 0B56 (equation-projection-formula-map); application to the ringed diagram site

proof.text: The theorem [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact] gives the proper-factor square for shift $[1]$, for arbitrary $J_jM,N$, with the canonical signed tensor and adjunction shifts. It gives all integer shifts as follows. The $r=0$ square is the identity equation. Paste the $[1]$ square at $N[r]$ with the $[r]$ square at $N$; the coherent shift-addition identifications turn their composite into the $[r+1]$ square. For the negative generator, apply the $[1]$ square at $N[-1]$, shift by $[-1]$, and cancel the invertible shift comparisons, using $[1][-1]\cong[0]$; this gives the $[-1]$ square. Iterate it for negative $r$. The canonical cochain comparisons used here are coherent: on first degree $a$ their tensor signs obey $(-1)^{(r+s)a}=(-1)^{ra}(-1)^{sa}$. This proves the proper-factor assertion without invertibility of $\pi$.

source.place: Tags 0B56 (equation-projection-formula-map), 07A4; iteration of the canonical cochain shift square

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-open-system-tensor-shift] on $\overline X$ with first input $M$ and second input $P_{p_c}N$. It applies to the actual quotient ring system and to arbitrary unbounded inputs. It gives the open-factor square for every integer $r$, with sign $(-1)^{ra}$ on a tensor summand of first degree $a$. Precompose this square by $P_{p_c}$ and apply $S_{p_c}$; [lem-weil-pbc-commshift-nattrans-comp-whisker] gives the square for the middle arrow $S_{p_c}(\delta)$ with precisely the composite shift comparisons.

source.place: Tag 0GL1 (lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor), signed second-slot square on the diagram site

proof.text: Let $\theta:P_jP_{p_c}\xrightarrow{\sim}P_f$ be the specified compositor. By [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] these inverse images are exact termwise; [lem-sf-integral-compactification-system-realization] specifies the canonical composition maps as derived classes of the maps on system complexes. On a representative $N^\bullet$, $\theta$ in degree $b$ is the ordinary inverse-image composition isomorphism on $N^b$. After shifting by $r$, both routes are that same component on $N^{b+r}$, and both differentials have multiplier $(-1)^r$. Hence $\theta$ commutes with $[r]$ already on system complexes. Tensoring with $M$ gives the same sign $(-1)^{ra}$ on both routes in first degree $a$; applying $J_j$ and $S_{p_c}$ gives the square for the last arrow. These equalities pass to derived classes because the specified comparisons are those derived classes.

source.place: Tag 0D6D (lemma-derived-pullback-composition), computation on representatives; Tag 07A4 tensor convention

proof.text:
Write the three displayed factors as $a_N,b_N,c_N$ and their intermediate composite shift comparisons as $s_0,s_1,s_2,s_3$, with $s_0=s_F^{(r)}$ and $s_3=s_H^{(r)}$. The preceding squares give $s_1a_{N[r]}=a_N[r]s_0$, $s_2b_{N[r]}=b_N[r]s_1$, and $s_3c_{N[r]}=c_N[r]s_2$. Substitute in succession:
$$s_3c_{N[r]}b_{N[r]}a_{N[r]}=c_N[r]b_N[r]a_N[r]s_0=(c_Nb_Na_N)[r]s_0.$$
This is the required equation since the specified system projection is $cba$. Composition and reassociation preserve the indicated shifts by [lem-weil-pbc-commshift-nattrans-comp-whisker]. Every equality above was in the system derived category, with its actual transitions. Restricting the inputs to normalized bounded constructible finite-Tor systems therefore gives the stated special case; no evaluation, restriction of scalars or total inverse limit has been used.
